title: Test Day Checklist
summary: What to bring, what happens at the test centre and how both parts of ADI part 1 work.

blocks.title: Bring with you
items: Northern Ireland licence: the photocard and paper counterpart.
Paper licence: bring a valid passport too.
Changed your name? Bring proof, like a marriage certificate or deed poll.

blocks.title: No licence, no test
blocks.text: Your test will be cancelled and you won't get your money back if you don't take the right things with you.

blocks.title: At the test centre
items: Arrive 15 minutes before the test starts: late means cancelled.
Turn off phones, smart watches and fitness trackers before you go in.
Put your belongings in a locker (or the clear box you're given).
Expect identity and security checks: empty pockets, roll up sleeves, metal detector.
There's no waiting area for anyone who comes with you.

blocks.title: Multiple choice
items: 100 questions in 1 hour 30 minutes, 25 in each of 4 bands.
Instructions and a practice question first.
You can flag questions and change any answer.
You can take a break of up to 3 minutes before hazard perception.

blocks.title: Hazard perception
items: 14 clips: each has at least one developing hazard, one has two.
Up to 5 points per developing hazard: click as soon as it starts.
Clicking continuously or in a pattern scores nothing.
One attempt per clip. Pass mark: 57 out of 75.

blocks.title: Reading difficulty?
blocks.text: Say so when you book. You can ask for an English voiceover, and send proof to DVSA to ask for more time on the multiple-choice part.
